messages:
anya: RFC follow-up: proposing we explicitly disentangle 'shim' ownership across layers — eng-platform owns API-facing compatibility shims (enveloping, request-normalizers, SDK helpers), eng-infra owns runtime/transport shims (sidecars, websocket/frame adapters). Need migration plan + telemetry so we can measure impact before flip.

sam: +1 on the split, but worried about duplication and who ships hotfixes. also rollout order — we should avoid flipping both at once.

lee: we had this pattern in a prior cutover. key is a tiny contract doc + CI e2e that verifies parity. otherwise we get subtle regressions.

maria: telemetry requirements: (a) which shim variant handled a request, (b) latency delta compared to baseline, (c) fallback counts and error-mode reasons. without those metrics we can't evaluate.

anya: rough migration plan i sketched:
1) add header for visibility: X-Redwood-Shim: <owner>/<version>
2) per-tenant opt-in toggle (featureflag) so customers opt into new owner behavior
3) shadow/dual-run for 48h (requests forked to new shim, responses ignored but validated)
4) canary rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated checks
5) rollback runbook + circuit breaker if error budget exceeded

sam: header sounds good. where does header->implementation mapping live? gateway config or service discovery? centralizing reduces drift.

lee: central gateway config + a tiny published JSON contract. also add a compatibility-test job that pulls a small set of recorded requests and asserts token-by-token/structured equality where possible.

maria: i'll make dashboards. sample prometheus-ish queries we should capture: 
- shim_requests_total{shim_owner=~".*"} by (shim_owner)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(shim_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, shim_owner))
- rate(shim_fallbacks_total[5m])
store tags: tenant_id, route, model, shim_owner, shim_version

anya: example header snippet we can standardize: 
```
X-Redwood-Shim: platform/2026-03-22-01
X-Redwood-Shim-Mode: shadow|canary|active
```

sam: runbook note: during canary, auto-trigger rollback if 5xx increase > 1% absolute OR p95 latency regresses > 150ms for 3 consecutive 5m windows.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary pipeline scheduled by eng-platform at 1722224000 for initial 5% cohort. refs: pipeline/compat-canary-1722.

maria: for compliance: ensure header doesn't leak PII. add audit that strips or hashes tenant-identifying fields on logs forwarded to third-party observability.

anya: open question for debate: who publishes the small conversion libs used by SDKs vs the runtime adapters used in sidecars? my proposal: platform publishes and maintains SDK-facing libs (JS/Go/python), infra maintains runtime adapters that run in the serving path. rationale: SDKs are API contract surface; runtime adapters need low-level infra change privileges.

sam: agree with that split. also add "compat test vectors" to the SDK packages so downstream clients can run quick sanity checks.

lee: i'll draft the CI jobs to run the vectors and wire new metrics. will have a PR by EOD tomorrow.

anya: thanks all — i'll update the RFC with this plan and link PRs here. ping me if you want items pulled into on-call runbook. :thumbsup:
